title: playable-screen-vtx-hazard-on-vs-off
queue_order: One binary, d50bf5c47c (the step 3 proof runs' ref; master's defaults merged at 4caff4a413, so the three NFS switches are on in both arms). Env-only A/B per title: ON queues --env HAKUX_VTX_HAZARD=1, OFF queues no --env. Scope and request shapes are fastpaths1010's screen as nfsdefault1011-screen.json lists it: 38 titles, 10 with a named route (300 s, no --frames-every) and 28 as a soak to the title screen (180 s, --frames-every 15). Call of Duty 3 is not on the Nova; the five owner-deferred titles and RalliSport stay off. One run per arm per title. Batch 1 is the 10 route titles (they reach play, where draws are densest); batches 2 and 3 are the soak titles, about 10 titles each. Each batch is read before the next is queued. HAKUX_RELEASE_PRIO=1, ON then OFF per title. No other default-off switch is headed for default-on in an active lane (hakux-lane-* units at 18:00 PDT: snapshot1011, soakvideo1011, this one), so the ON arm carries this switch alone.
judge: per title, docs/lanes/gtasagpu1011/scrread.py <run dirs>: fatal (title_verdict.judge crash/void), on-line (the 'HAKUX_VTX_HAZARD=<v>' logcat line: 1 ON, 0 OFF), finishes (the last 'vtx_hazard: N finishes' line, ON only), hdd (golden_status/state/loaded, errors flagged), gfps (g_fps_mean_reported_not_judged), frames (stills, read by eye ON against OFF). A title fails on an ON-only fatal, an ON-only hdd error, an ON-only visual defect in the stills, or an ON gfps more than 3% below OFF where finishes > 0. A failing title is rerun twice (one pair each) before anything is attributed to the switch. A title with finishes = 0 drew exactly what OFF draws (the switch only adds a finish before an upload that changes bytes an earlier draw reads), so a gap there is the run, not the switch.
baseline: fastpaths1010's screen passed all 38 with its toggle; nfsdefault1011 screened the 10 route titles with the NFS switches (all pass; Kabuki Warriors not judged, #787 stall placement, owner). Both arms here run those defaults.
prediction: None of the 38 fail (P 0.85). The switch changes nothing but the submit points: byte-exact with a deferred finish in the dumps (NOTES 2c), and five ON-arm GTA SA dump runs plus the two proof soaks ran without a fatal. Most titles show finishes = 0 or a few: GTA SA's 100-370 per 10 s comes from rewriting one vertex buffer for several immediate-mode draws a frame, which is a pattern, not the rule. What would refute it: an ON-only crash/hang/abort, an ON-only hdd error, an ON-only visual defect, or an ON gfps more than 3% below OFF in a title where the switch acted.
expect_note: fail_titles starts empty: the claim is that no scoped title fails. A 'title not on device' moves a title to not_run. A confirmed failure gets a 'WIDEN: <reason>' line in docs/lanes/gtasagpu1011/NOTES.md naming the title, the column and the result ids.
